name: OpenChamber

runner.notes: Install OpenCode CLI (desktop bundles a matching OpenCode CLI), then run the OpenChamber desktop app or `openchamber --ui-password <pw>` (web/PWA on localhost:3000). Connect one provider/model in Settings -> Providers, open only runs/<run-id>/worktree as the project (or a worktree session created from it), send prompt.md in a single session, then harness-verify on the actual session cwd. Record OpenChamber version (e.g. 2.0.1), OpenCode version, provider/model, whether a worktree session/Multi-run/Session Goals were used, and interventions (approvals, answered questions). Headless path: CLI/server with OPENCODE_HOST pointing at a pinned OpenCode server.

inclusion: Direct Class A local/self-hosted ADE: independent open-source workspace (desktop, web/PWA, VS Code, iOS/Android, CLI/server) layered on the OpenCode agent server, with parallel sessions, git worktree sessions, Multi-run across up to five models, Session Goals, diff walkthrough review, GitHub PR flows, schedules, and E2E-encrypted remote access.
runtime_model_notes: Official README: uses OpenCode to run coding agents and is not affiliated with the OpenCode team; agent loop is the OpenCode server (managed or external via OPENCODE_HOST). Model breadth comes from OpenCode providers, not multiple guest CLIs.
pricing_model: Free and open source (MIT). Bring-your-own model provider keys/subscriptions via OpenCode. Patreon support link; Private Relay is operated by OpenChamber (self-hostable relay repo exists). No paid tier found in official sources this pass.
public_stack_signals: Official site/README: open-source ADE for running and reviewing AI coding work on desktop, web, VS Code, and mobile; independent of the OpenCode team.

research.positioning: An independent, open-source agentic development environment that wraps the OpenCode agent server with a multi-surface workspace (desktop, web/PWA, VS Code, mobile, CLI/server) for running parallel and goal-driven coding sessions, isolating them in git worktrees, reviewing changes, shipping via GitHub, and steering work remotely.

runtime: OpenCode server (managed by OpenChamber or external via OPENCODE_HOST)
frontend: VS Code extension (also listed for Cursor, Windsurf, Trae on site)
backend: Express-based server with WebSocket and PTY terminals (npm dependencies)
simple-git and Octokit for git/GitHub flows
Private Relay (openchamber-relay: Cloudflare Worker + Durable Object, self-hostable)
data: local-first: projects and sessions stay on the operator machine (official site claim)
provider config and keys written to OpenCode config/auth
git worktrees for isolated sessions (location chosen per worktree; default suggested from branch name)
unknowns: Exact on-disk layout for OpenChamber state and default worktree root not verified in this pass.
Hosted Private Relay operational limits/SLA and any future paid tiers not published.

Depth of third-party CLI support: provider plugins (opencode-claude, opencode-cursor) are OpenCode provider plugins, not separate guest CLIs; no official evidence it drives Claude Code/Codex CLIs directly.

infrastructure: Local-first: OpenChamber server binds to 127.0.0.1 by default and starts or connects to an OpenCode server on the operator machine.
Clients (desktop, web/PWA, VS Code, mobile) connect to that server directly, over LAN/VPN, SSH remote instances, Cloudflare/Ngrok tunnels, or the E2E-encrypted Private Relay.
Model/API traffic goes through OpenCode to the user's configured providers with the user's own keys.

agent_support: any OpenCode provider/model, incl. API-key and device-flow sign-in providers
named agents with default model and permissions
orchestration: parallel sessions across projects with working/waiting/finished/failed status
Multi-run: same task to up to five models, compare, Fusion to combine
Session Goals: auto-continue until goal met, blocked, or limit
agent control tool to create/fork sessions and worktree sessions from chat
workspace_isolation: git worktree sessions (new or existing branch)
Integrate worktree commits into another branch with agent conflict resolution
review_shipping: diff review and Changes Walkthrough (AI-guided ordered steps)
commit, push, create PR, update and merge PR
start sessions from GitHub issues/PRs; send failed checks/review comments back to agent
Preview / built-in browser with element-to-agent context
remote_mobile: Private Relay with QR pairing and revocable device tokens
SSH remote machines, LAN, tunnels, reverse proxy
reattach to running terminal from another device
context_memory: sessions and projects persist across devices
notes, todos, plans, and reusable project actions
skills and skills catalog, magic prompts, commands/snippets
usage view: provider limits, token use, costs
integrations: VS Code / Cursor / Windsurf / Trae extension

install_surface: curl install script + `openchamber` CLI (Node.js 22+, OpenCode CLI installed)
at least one provider/model connected in OpenCode
parity_risks: Single guest runtime (OpenCode): correctness reflects OpenCode + chosen model more than OpenChamber (runtime_model guest-cli).
Session Goals auto-continue and Multi-run/Fusion change turn counts and model mix; disable or record explicitly.
Worktree sessions run outside runs/<run-id>/worktree unless opened directly; verify the actual session cwd.
Managed vs external OpenCode server versions can differ between desktop bundle and CLI install; pin and record.
Relay/tunnel/mobile paths are not parity-equivalent to local-only runs.

hypotheses: Becoming the default GUI/control plane for OpenCode users across every surface.
Goal-driven and comparative execution (Session Goals, Multi-run + Fusion) differentiates from plain chat UIs.
E2E relay + native mobile apps make remote steering low-friction.
evidence: README and site document multi-surface workspace, Session Goals, Multi-run/Fusion, Changes Walkthrough, GitHub flows, Private Relay.
Docs describe worktree sessions, isolate-runs Multi-run, OpenCode server management, and agent control tool.
Release v2.0.1 ships desktop (3 OSes), Android, VS Code vsix, and web tarball; ~10.6K GitHub stars at review; MIT license.
unknowns: Dependence on a single third-party runtime (OpenCode) and its API stability is an unscored risk.
Head-to-head orchestration quality vs Paseo/Emdash/Orca is unscored.
Governance/maintainer bus factor (single named author in LICENSE/package.json) not assessed.
